rows.item: Sirius FM-4 communications satellite (flight-ready backup, never launched)
rows.notes: Museum page: on display in One World Connected.

rows.item: Dove satellite (early-generation flight unit donated by Planet Labs)
rows.notes: Museum page says 'early generation flight unit', on display in One World Connected; not stated whether it flew, so recorded as unflown flight-standard unit.

rows.item: Iridium first prototype satellite built by Motorola (engineering and flight components)
rows.notes: On display in One World Connected, but it is a first-generation Iridium prototype, not an Iridium NEXT unit; operator to decide if it counts for this ref.

rows.item: Skylab Orbital Workshop, backup flight unit
rows.notes: Museum page: on display in RTX Living in the Space Age Hall.

rows.item: GPS-0012, Block II Qualification Test Vehicle (never flew)
rows.notes: Evidence is the ION museum page (undated); current display at SDASM not confirmed on the museum's own site.

rows.item: NTS-2 engineering model (restored; GPS precursor satellite)
rows.notes: Displayed in the 2013 'Time and Navigation' exhibition; whether it is on display after NASM's renovation is unconfirmed. NTS-2 is a GPS precursor, not a Block I Navstar. Page returned 403 to my fetch, so the claim rests on search-result text.
ESA page only says (Dec 1999) the model was ready to be moved to the Guiana Spaceport Museum for display; current display not confirmed.
